_about: PZB01G only. Two changes, both to OUR rendering rather than to the source.
The 'Yes - ' prefix is the shape of the QUESTION — 'do you regard yourself as
belonging to any particular religion?' — not a fact about the person. A
persona reading 'Religion: Yes - Roman Catholic' is not a sentence about
anyone. Stripped. The religions themselves are untouched.
Faith names are given as the adjective a person would use of themselves
('Muslim', not 'Islam'), because a persona says what someone IS. Note the
source mixes both conventions: 'Yes - Baptist' beside 'Yes - Islam'.
One label uses an en dash where the rest use a hyphen ('Yes – Orthodox
Christian'); both are handled, since typography normalises and wording does
not.
NOTHING IS COLLAPSED HERE, deliberately. There is one scheme, so there is no
second vocabulary to reconcile against and no pressure to coarsen. Rolling the
denominations up to the ONS religion groups, or the tenures up to own/rent,
would destroy detail nobody has asked us to lose in exchange for a comparability
that does not yet have a second party. When UKHLS arrives with its own variables
— and it will, SN 6849 carries both — that is the moment to decide the canonical,
with both schemes in view. Designing it now from one scheme risks exactly the
one-way-street problem in persona/categories.py: a canonical fixed too early
cannot be made finer later.
